added.title: Environmental Health/Emergency Management Program Director
added.description:
Apply

Description

Great Lakes Inter-Tribal Council is a non-profit organization formed by the Native American Tribes of Wisconsin. We serve all WI tribes by providing administration of grant-funded programs either directly or with sub grants. Programs range from Child and Maternal services to Education to Disability and Elder benefits. Our Mission is: To Enhance the Quality of Life for all Native People.

Position Summary

The Environmental Health/Emergency Management (EH/EM) Program Director provides leadership and oversight for the Great Lakes Inter-Tribal Epidemiology Center's (GLITEC’s) environmental health and emergency management program. Responsibilities include directing the planning, implementation, coordination, and evaluation of EH/EM workplans, projects, technical assistance, and related grant activities across the Bemidji Area. Working as a member of the GLITEC leadership team, this position supervises and supports EH/EM staff; coordinates environmental health, emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience activities; develops and maintains partnerships with Tribal Nations and other partners; and ensures program activities are responsive to Tribal priorities and needs. The position uses public health, environmental health, emergency management, project management, data, and relationship-management skills to advance program priorities. Frequent travel is required to meet the needs of the position. This position will be located in our Madison, Wisconsin office or our Green Bay, Wisconsin office.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Direct the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of environmental health and emergency management program workplans, projects, technical assistance, and grant-funded activities.
Develop and maintain partnerships with Tribal Nations, Tribal programs, Urban Indian Organizations, Indian Health Service, and other federal, state, local, academic, and community partners to support environmental health and emergency management priorities throughout the Bemidji Area.
Provide program leadership for strategic planning, budgeting, grant implementation, resource allocation, and development of environmental health and emergency management services and initiatives.
Provide leadership and technical guidance on environmental health and emergency management priorities, including environmental hazards and exposures, drinking water and lead, emerging contaminants, climate-related health risks, emergency preparedness, response, recovery, resilience, and risk communication.
Develop and maintain program performance, evaluation, and reporting mechanisms to measure progress, outcomes, technical assistance, and service delivery and to inform continuous program improvement.
Guide the use of environmental health and emergency management data, assessments, mapping, dashboards, surveillance, environmental scans, and other quantitative and qualitative information to identify priorities and support Tribal decision-making.
Coordinate with GLITEC communications staff and subject matter experts to develop and disseminate environmental health, emergency preparedness, risk communication, and public health education resources.
Plan and oversee program trainings, exercises, meetings, webinars, conferences, workgroups, and other learning or preparedness activities.
Provide and oversee technical assistance to Tribal Nations and other eligible partners related to environmental health, emergency management, preparedness planning, assessment, implementation, evaluation, and capacity building.
Work with Tribal leaders, health departments, emergency management programs, environmental programs, and other partners to identify priorities and develop culturally responsive approaches that strengthen community health, preparedness, and resilience.
Represent GLITEC and actively participate in environmental health and emergency management committees, task teams, workgroups, partnerships, and policy or program initiatives, as assigned.
Oversee contracts, subawards, consultants, vendors, and other program resources as needed to accomplish EH/EM program activities.
Prepare, review, and ensure timely submission of required program, grant, performance, and other reports in coordination with GLITEC leadership and administrative staff.
Supervise, mentor, and support assigned environmental health and emergency management staff; establish priorities, coordinate workloads, support professional development, and promote effective collaboration across the EH/EM program and GLITEC.
Work with GLITEC Director and other GLITEC leadership to provide overall program advisement and ensure EH/EM activities are coordinated with broader GLITEC public health services.

Additional Duties And Responsibilities

Maintain a working knowledge of GLITEC grants, programs, and services that intersect with environmental health and emergency management.
Remain current on environmental health, emergency preparedness, response, recovery, resilience, risk communication, and relevant public health data, guidance, resources, and emerging issues affecting American Indian/Alaska Native communities.
Assure all services are delivered in a culturally responsive manner that respects Tribal sovereignty, priorities, customs, traditions, values, and beliefs.
Participate on environmental health, emergency management, public health, and other committees and workgroups within and outside the organization, as assigned.
Attend all training sessions and meetings as scheduled.
Attend conferences, trainings, exercises, and professional development activities to remain current on advances and emerging practices in environmental health, emergency management, and Tribal public health.
Participate in assessments, evaluation, research, and data projects related to environmental health and emergency management as designated by the GLITEC Director.
Perform other duties as necessary to fulfill the responsibilities of this position.

Working Relationships And Scope

Reports directly to the GLITEC Director and works under limited supervision. Receives guidance on broad program goals, priorities, and policy and has responsibility for directing assigned environmental health and emergency management program activities and achieving program objectives. Provides day-to-day leadership and supervision to assigned EH/EM staff and works collaboratively with other GLITEC program directors, epidemiologists, public health specialists, communications staff, and administrative staff. Maintains frequent contact with Tribal Nations, Urban Indian Organizations, Indian Health Service, and federal, state, local, academic, and community partners to coordinate projects, provide and obtain information, and advance environmental health and emergency management priorities.

Performance Dimensions

Supports mission of Great Lakes Inter-Tribal Council, Inc. Demonstrate a basic understanding of tribal customs, traditions, values, and beliefs. Quality, quantity, accuracy, timeliness and thoroughness of work performed; quality of communications and development of good working relationships with others internal and external to the organization; honesty and integrity in the execution of all activities; customer satisfaction with services provided; maintain and comply with all GLITC policies and procedures; reliability in reporting to work regularly and on time; soundness of business decisions made; maintain the integrity of confidential business information; stay current in field and utilize that information where practical. Demonstrate a friendly and helpful approach and attitude to internal and external customers; professionalism; and commitment to the job.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Required: Master’s degree in public health, environmental health, emergency management, emergency preparedness, environmental science, health sciences, public administration, or a related field, and progressively responsible experience in environmental health, emergency management, public health, program management, or a related area. An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience may be considered consistent with organizational requirements. Demonstrated experience managing projects, programs, grants, staff, or multidisciplinary initiatives is required. Preferred: Experience working with American Indian/Alaska Native communities, Tribal Nations, Tribal organizations, or Tribal public health, environmental, or emergency management programs. Knowledge of Tribal sovereignty and the governmental and jurisdictional context in which Tribal environmental health and emergency management programs operate. Knowledge of environmental health practice, emergency preparedness and management, risk communication, public health systems, data-informed planning, and grant implementation. Individual must possess excellent verbal and written communication, leadership, supervision, project management, problem-solving, relationship-building, and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple priorities; ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team; and ability to communicate effectively with Tribal leaders, staff, community partners, and government agencies. Requires a high level of confidentiality. Must possess a valid driver’s license and/or reliable transportation with adequate insurance and ability to travel.

This is a full-time exempt position based on skills and experience, with a salary range of $70,000 - $75,000.
This position will be located in our Madison, Wisconsin office or our Green Bay, Wisconsin office.
This position is not a remote position.
The position includes the following benefits:
paid time off (PTO) in the form of annual and personal leave; paid holidays; insurance benefits including health, dental, life insurance, accidental death, and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, short-term (STD) and long-term (LTD) disability insurance; health savings account (HSA), flexible spending account (FSA), and 401(k) retirement plan. When traveling for work, eligible expenses are reimbursed based on GSA rates.
Drug and background check is required before hire.

To Apply:
See the employment page of our website at www.glitc.org for more information.

Great Lakes Inter Tribal Council does not respond to phone calls nor emails inquiries regarding the status of your application. Only the most qualified candidates will be contacted for an interview.

Live AI copilots or real-time text generators during an interview are strictly prohibited and will result in your disqualification.

As an equal opportunity employer, GLITC intends to comply fully with all federal and state laws and the information requested on this application will not be used for any purpose prohibited by law. Holders of the Environmental Scientist Advisor position will complete tasks such as:

Conduct professional studies in the groundwater program.
Review projects, documents, and applications for regulatory compliance.

Strong communication and organizational skills
Self-motivated with excellent time management skills
Strong technical writing skills
Strong skills in Geographic Information System (GIS)
Understanding water sampling procedures and data management.

Maintain a driver's license
Frequent communication in person or by other means required
Travel required
Field work may require standing, stooping, bending, and lifting at times.

added.title: Principal Toxicologist (REMOTE ROLE)
added.description:
Description

Principal Toxicologist

Job Description

To support ICF’s dynamic growth and expanding client base, we are seeking a highly accomplished Principal Toxicologist
to provide scientific leadership on complex human health hazard and risk assessment programs supporting federal agencies, including U.S. EPA and NIEHS. This position is within ICF’s Health Sciences Portfolio, a group of 100+ science professionals who provide toxicology, hazard assessment, epidemiology, risk assessment, exposure assessment, environmental modeling, and related support that addresses the full spectrum of potentially hazardous agents, including chemicals and microbes. We specialize in identifying and quantifying the effects of environmental pollutants—including metals, pesticides, industrial chemicals, and volatile organic compounds—on human health and the environment.

This is a senior scientific leadership position
intended for an established toxicologist with approximately 20+ years of experience
and recognized expertise in toxicology, human health risk assessment, mechanistic toxicology, and the interpretation and integration of complex scientific evidence.

The successful candidate will serve as a trusted scientific advisor and technical authority
, providing strategic direction on challenging toxicological and regulatory questions and helping shape scientifically defensible approaches to hazard identification, dose-response assessment, mode-of-action analysis, systematic review, and human health risk assessment.

A particular focus of the role will be advancing the integration of mechanistic toxicology, molecular biology, new approach methodologies (NAMs), and emerging scientific methods
into regulatory toxicology and risk assessment. The individual will provide expert interpretation of diverse evidence streams including epidemiological, animal, molecular, cellular, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, high-throughput screening, and other mechanistic data.

This individual will also mentor and guide multidisciplinary scientific teams, contribute to the development of innovative technical approaches, provide senior-level review of major scientific deliverables, and represent ICF in substantive technical discussions with federal clients and external scientific stakeholders.

Location: Remote

What You’ll Do…

Serve as a senior technical authority and subject matter expert on complex toxicological, human health risk assessment, and regulatory science issues.
Provide scientific leadership and strategic direction for major federal toxicology, hazard assessment, systematic review, and human health risk assessment programs.
Advise federal clients and project teams on the interpretation and integration of complex toxicological evidence and the application of evolving scientific methods to regulatory decision-making.
Develop and critically evaluate approaches for hazard identification, dose-response assessment, weight-of-evidence evaluation, mode-of-action analysis, and human health risk assessment.
Lead the integration of mechanistic toxicology and molecular biology data with traditional animal and human evidence, including NAMs, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, high-throughput screening, pathway-based data, and adverse outcome pathway frameworks.
Provide expert guidance on technically challenging or scientifically uncertain issues where established methods may not provide a clear answer.
Serve as a senior scientific reviewer for major technical reports, hazard assessments, risk assessments, systematic reviews, manuscripts, protocols, guidance documents, and regulatory science deliverables.
Lead or advise multidisciplinary teams of toxicologists, risk assessors, epidemiologists, biologists, statisticians, exposure scientists, and computational scientists addressing complex environmental health questions.
Design and oversee systematic review and evidence-integration approaches, including literature evaluation, study quality assessment, evidence synthesis, mechanistic data integration, and weight-of-evidence determinations.
Provide senior-level expertise in cancer and noncancer hazard assessment, including interpretation of mechanistic evidence relevant to carcinogenicity and other adverse health outcomes.
Provide scientific expertise concerning chemicals and emerging contaminants such as PFAS, PAHs, endocrine-active chemicals, pesticides, industrial chemicals, metals, and other environmental pollutants.
Develop innovative technical approaches and methodologies to address emerging scientific and regulatory challenges.
Lead technical discussions, briefings, and presentations with federal clients, scientific panels, external experts, and other stakeholders.
Provide scientific direction, mentorship, and technical review to senior, mid-level, and junior scientists and contribute to the development of ICF's next generation of technical leaders.
Contribute to strategic growth activities by developing technical approaches for proposals, identifying emerging areas of regulatory science, supporting client engagement, and helping position ICF for new scientific work.
Represent ICF's scientific capabilities through publications, presentations, technical workshops, scientific conferences, and other thought-leadership activities, as appropriate.

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in toxicology, pharmacology, environmental health sciences, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, or a closely related scientific discipline.
20+ years of experience in toxicology, human health risk assessment, regulatory science, environmental health, or a closely related field.

Additional Qualifications

Extensive experience conducting or leading hazard identification, toxicological evaluation, systematic review, weight-of-evidence analysis, mode-of-action analysis, or human health risk assessment.
Significant experience supporting U.S. EPA, NIEHS, or other federal environmental or public health programs.
Demonstrated expertise interpreting and integrating animal, human, mechanistic, molecular, and/or computational toxicology evidence.
Demonstrated experience providing senior scientific leadership and technical direction for complex scientific programs, assessments, or regulatory initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to communicate highly complex scientific concepts and conclusions clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Nationally recognized or demonstrated subject matter expertise in one or more areas of regulatory toxicology, mechanistic toxicology, human health risk assessment, carcinogenicity assessment, computational toxicology, or environmental health science.
Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT) or comparable advanced professional credential is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of federal approaches to hazard identification, dose-response assessment, systematic review, evidence integration, and human health risk assessment.
Extensive experience with mode-of-action (MOA), adverse outcome pathway (AOP), and biological pathway frameworks.
Expertise interpreting mechanistic and molecular data, including transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, high-throughput screening, molecular assays, cellular systems, and other NAMs.
Demonstrated ability to determine the biological and regulatory relevance of mechanistic evidence and integrate it with epidemiological and animal toxicology evidence.
Expertise in cancer hazard assessment and carcinogenic mode-of-action analysis.
Experience evaluating PFAS, endocrine disruptors, PAHs, pesticides, industrial chemicals, emerging contaminants, or other environmentally relevant agents.
Advanced understanding of systematic review methodologies and evidence-integration frameworks used in environmental health and regulatory science.
Experience with dose-response analysis, benchmark dose modeling, quantitative risk assessment, pathway enrichment analysis, or related quantitative methodologies.
Demonstrated record of developing or advancing scientific methods, frameworks, guidance, or technical approaches.
Strong record of peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, scientific presentations, regulatory assessments, or other evidence of scientific leadership.
Experience serving as a technical advisor to federal clients, scientific panels, peer-review groups, or other senior scientific stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and provide scientific mentorship to experienced scientists.
Experience developing technical approaches for major federal proposals, task orders, or scientific programs.

Working at ICF

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future.

We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer. Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy.

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Work Authorization and Sponsorship

All candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. This position is not eligible for new H-1B visa sponsorship by ICF. Candidates who currently hold valid work authorization may be considered for a change of employer petition, subject to company policy and applicable immigration requirements.

Reasonable Accommodations

Reasonable Accommodations are available, including, but not limited to, for disabled veterans, individuals with disabilities, and individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs, in all phases of the application and employment process. To request an accommodation, please email Candidateaccommodation@icf.com and we will be happy to assist. All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent required to provide needed reasonable accommodations. 

Read more about workplace discrimination rights or our benefit offerings which are included in the Transparency in (Benefits) Coverage Act.

Bot and Third-Party Applications

Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration. Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact Candidateaccommodation@icf.com for assistance.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

At ICF, we are committed to ensuring a fair interview process for all candidates based on their own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is not permitted. This policy is in place to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the interview process. 

However, we understand that some candidates may require accommodation that involves the use of AI. If such an accommodation is needed, candidates are instructed to contact us in advance at candidateaccommodation@icf.com. We are dedicated to providing the necessary support to ensure that all candidates have an equal opportunity to succeed.  

Pay Range

There are multiple factors that are considered in determining final pay for a position, including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, certifications and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location, education and certifications as well as contract provisions regarding labor categories that are specific to the position.

added.title: West-Side Alternative Treatment (AMPS) Lead Permit Writer (Environmental Specialist 4)
added.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a West-Side Alternative Treatment (AMPS) Lead Permit Writer (Environmental Specialist 4)
within the Nuclear Waste Program .

Location:

Richland Field Office in Richland, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
Initially, this position requires working in the office five days a week for onboarding and training. After successful completion, a partial telework schedule may be established with supervisor approval.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by November 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

As the West-Side Alternative Treatment (AMPS) Lead Permit Writer, you will serve as the regulatory expert for permitting activities associated with the 200 West AMPS and Grouting treatment facility. In this role, you will help ensure the safe treatment and management of highly hazardous waste through complex permitting reviews and regulatory oversight. You will work closely with technical experts, the U.S. Department of Energy, Environmental Protection Agency, other partner agencies, and contractors to support sound environmental decisions.

This position offers the opportunity to work on one of the most complex and high-profile environmental cleanup projects in the country. Together with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and chemists, you will provide expertise on challenging regulatory and technical issues and help shape permitting decisions for a unique treatment system. The role provides opportunities to expand your experience in environmental permitting, hazardous waste management, regulatory interpretation, public engagement, and team coordination while contributing to work that protects human health and the environment.

What You Will Do

Serve as the primary permit writer and regulatory expert for the 200 West AMPS and Grouting treatment facility.
Review permit applications, modifications, and technical documents to ensure compliance with state and federal requirements.
Evaluate complex technical and regulatory issues and develop permitting recommendations and permit conditions.
Coordinate reviews with engineers, chemists, and other technical specialists to support permitting actions.
Collaborate with the Double-Shell Tank (DST) regulatory lead to ensure connected systems are covered by appropriate regulatory requirements.
Represent the Nuclear Waste Program in meetings with the U.S. Department of Energy, Environmental Protection Agency, contractors, and partner agencies.
Respond to public comments and present technical and regulatory information to the public and other interested groups.
Conduct site visits and inspections to assess compliance with permit requirements and engineering specifications.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine (9) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:

Regulatory Interpretation and Compliance – Ability to independently interpret federal and state environmental regulations and apply them to facility operations, permitting decisions, and compliance evaluations.
Permit Development and Review – Ability to evaluate, develop, and negotiate complex environmental permits to ensure regulatory compliance and protect human health and the environment.
Field Inspections and Technical Assessments – Ability to independently conduct environmental field inspections, construction oversight, or technical site assessments to verify compliance with permits, engineering specifications, and regulatory standards.
Critical and Analytical Thinking – Ability to apply critical and analytical thinking to evaluate complex information and determine appropriate courses of action to support sound regulatory and permitting decisions.
Information Review and Assessment – Ability to review and assess technical information and data to draw accurate conclusions and recommend decisions or actions that ensure compliance and program effectiveness.
Research and Data Analysis – Ability to conduct research and analyze qualitative and quantitative data to provide evidence-based support for regulatory interpretations, permit conditions, and decision-making.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or closely related field.

Examples Of How To Qualify

9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.
2 years of experience AND a Ph.D.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must meet the U.S. Department of Energy requirements to obtain and maintain a USDOE badge for access to the Hanford Site.
Must take and pass HAZWOPER training (initial 40-hour training) within the first six months of employment, and 8-hour refresher training annually.

Desired Qualifications

Environmental Remediation Knowledge – Ability to apply principles, practices, and methods of environmental remediation to ensure accurate evaluation of cleanup actions and support effective regulatory oversight.

Job Description

Only applicants who meet the Minimum Qualification Requirements and meet all selective requirements (listed below) will be placed on the

eligible list.

The Department of Natural Resources encourages all applicants to upload a current resume and cover letter to their online application.

Join the Iowa Department of Natural Resources Conservation and Recreation Division to coordinate sovereign lands construction permits and environmental reviews, utilizing spatial analysis and field surveys to support natural resource management across the state.

This position plays a central role in balancing natural resource protection with regulatory compliance by managing Environmental Review requests and Sovereign Land Construction Permit applications. In this role, you will evaluate proposed projects, coordinate closely with DNR Floodplains and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and serve as a primary liaison for applicants, consulting engineers, and the public through meetings, formal correspondence, and community hearings. Alongside permitting oversight, you will contribute directly to environmental policy development by researching complex issues, and presenting recommendations to agency leadership.

In the field and behind the scenes, you will assist biological investigations that drive data management for state conservation efforts. You will conduct ecological, botanical, and zoological field surveys, and analyze species and habitat data. Additionally, you will leverage GIS, database tools, and web applications to maintain and enhance the Iowa Natural Areas Inventory (INAI), translating vital plant and wildlife records into spatial analyses, maps, and reporting tools that inform conservation decisions across the division.

Essential Functions

Process incoming Environmental Review (ER) requests and Sovereign Land Construction Permit applications in compliance with applicable state, federal, and local standards and align permit actions with Floodplain Management regulations, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and related environmental regulatory bodies.
Develop and maintain effective working relationships with staff, other state and federal agencies, environmental interests, industry professionals and local stakeholders.
Confer with permit applicants, developers, and consulting engineers via meetings, email, and formal correspondence; identify application deficiencies, recommend amendments, draft conditional approval or denial determinations, and prescribe necessary mitigation/follow-up actions.
Utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to process survey data, conduct spatial analyses, and generate cartographic products, spatial layers, and technical documentation for state parks, preserves, and public land management plans.
Maintain, enhance, and ensure data integrity of the Iowa Natural Areas Inventory (INAI) database; review, input, modify, and QC species location, population status, and community survey records.
Analyze field observations, biological data, and state/federal statutory requirements to evaluate ecological impacts and project viability and author comprehensive resource reports detailing plant and animal communities, habitat assessments, impact evaluations, and recommended land management practices.
Develop, read, and comprehend laws, rules, policies, technical documents and position papers and effectively communicate them orally and in writing.
Plan and perform comprehensive field surveys to locate, document, and evaluate rare, threatened, endangered, and sensitive species and natural plant/wildlife communities.

The Successful Candidate Must Be Able To

Produce quality work products in a timely manner.
Work independently with consistent results and minimal supervision.
Adjust to change, work pressures, or difficult situations without undue stress; some travel across the state as required.
Demonstrate initiative, a customer service focus and display high standards of ethical conduct.

Critical Job Competencies

Accountability, Integrity, High Productivity, Communication Skills, Team Player, Interpersonal Skills, Customer Focus, Self-Management, Technical Skills (GIS, Web-Based Applications)

What You Get From Us

Selectives

230 Geographic Information Systems (Department of Natural Resources)

18 semester hours of education or 1 year of experience that demonstrates the applicant has competencies in the following areas:

Ability to create, edit, import, export, project, and georeference GIS data.
Demonstrated proficiency with the major ESRI software products. These products include ArcView, ArcInfo, ArcGIS.
Utilize user-developed and/or ESRI scripts and extensions for incorporation and utilization in projects.
Ability to conduct spatial analyses and queries in order to answer complex questions relating to spatial data.
Ability to produce cartographic documents which clearly present outputs from spatial analyses. Document formats should at a minimum include hardcopy as well as the following digital formats .pdf, .tif, and .jpg.
Ability to work with, or train, others to use GIS to attain a common goal

Applicant must provide specific work examples to demonstrate each of the competencies. The examples should include a thorough explanation of the project goal, the process utilized and the result of the process.

054 Biological Sciences

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's Degree in natural science; an equivalent combination of experience and education substituting one year of full-time professional work in an environmental, radiation control, environmental health or food sanitation program for each year (30 semester hours) of the required education.
